notes.meaning: Paul writes from prison, where he is held for serving Christ and sharing the good news with the nations. He urges believers to live in a way that matches the high calling God gave them. Our daily conduct should be an expression of thankfulness for the salvation we have freely received.

Living worthy of God's call begins with quiet humility, gentleness, and patient love toward others. Instead of reacting quickly to offenses, believers are called to bear with each other's weaknesses. True peace is a gift created by the Holy Spirit, and Christians must work hard to guard and maintain it.

All believers across the world belong to a single spiritual body, the church, which is brought to life by the one Holy Spirit. Every Christian also shares the same glorious hope of eternal life with God. Because of these shared realities, believers have every reason to stand together as one family.

The church is united under one Master, Jesus Christ, through one shared trust in Him. Believers are also marked by one baptism, which openly shows their shared commitment to Christ and welcomes them into His people.

differ.view: Water baptism by immersion is the one outward ordinance of baptism commanded for believers who profess faith in Christ.
The one baptism is the spiritual washing that joins a person to Christ, which water baptism signs and seals once for all, so baptism is never to be repeated even if received in infancy.
The verse speaks of water baptism as the outward sign of salvation common to all believers, which does not exclude a later baptism in the Holy Spirit for power in service.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Most scholars agree that Paul refers primarily to water baptism as the universal rite of initiation that welcomed all believers into the Christian community.

notes.meaning: There is only one God, who is the loving Father of all who trust in Christ. He rules supreme over everything, works His purposes through all things, and lives within all His people by His Spirit. This single divine Father unites the entire church under His loving care.

While all Christians share in the same salvation, Christ gives individual spiritual gifts to each person in different ways. No believer is left out, and no one receives these abilities by earning them. Each person receives just what Christ chooses to give, so everyone can help the church grow.

Paul quotes Psalm 68 to show that Christ acted like a victorious king after winning a battle. When Jesus rose back to heaven, He triumphed over Satan, sin, and death, taking captive the powers that once held us. From His place of victory, He showered spiritual gifts upon His people.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars note that the original Hebrew of Psalm 68:18 speaks of receiving gifts from people, but Paul may have adapted the wording or used an early Christian tradition to highlight Christ giving gifts to His church.

notes.meaning: Before Christ ascended high above all the heavens, He first came down to this lowly world. The very same Jesus who humbled Himself to take on human flesh and die is now exalted to the highest place of honor. From that supreme throne, He fills the whole universe with His presence and power.

differ.view: Christ descending to the lower parts of the earth refers to the incarnation, where He humbled Himself to live on this earthly world, rather than a journey to the realm of the dead.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The descent to the lower parts of the earth is understood to include Christ visiting the realm of the dead to announce deliverance to the souls waiting there.

notes.meaning: Christ Himself gave gifted leaders to guide and care for His people. He provided apostles and prophets to lay the foundation of the faith, evangelists to preach the good news to the lost, and pastors and teachers to shepherd and instruct congregations. These leaders are personal gifts from Christ to nurture His church.

differ.view: The foundational offices of apostle and prophet belonged to the first generation of the church and ceased once the Scriptures and the foundation were complete.
While the original revelatory role of the twelve apostles ended, ongoing apostolic and prophetic ministry functions continue to be provided by the Holy Spirit today.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern groups teach that God is currently restoring the formal governing offices of apostle and prophet in a fivefold ministry structure necessary for church perfection.

notes.meaning: God gave these leaders to train and prepare ordinary Christians for practical acts of service. The work of ministry does not belong only to a few, but to every believer. As each person serves, the whole body of Christ becomes stronger and better established.

The continuing goal of this ministry is that all believers arrive at complete agreement in what they believe and grow in personal knowledge of God's Son. Christian growth means leaving spiritual immaturity behind and becoming more like Jesus. The ultimate goal is to reach the full, mature stature that reflects Christ Himself.

God wants His people to stop acting like small children who are easily confused and led astray. Immature believers are like tiny boats tossed around by stormy waves whenever new or deceptive teachings blow through. Being rooted in God's truth protects Christians from clever deceivers who scheme to mislead them.

Instead of falling for lies, believers must hold firmly to the truth while treating others with genuine love. Christ is the head of the church, and every member is closely joined to Him and to each other like parts of a healthy human body. When every individual part does its assigned work, the entire church grows stronger and builds itself up in love.

Paul solemnly commands Christians to leave behind the empty, foolish ways of thinking practiced by the unbelieving world. Unbelievers live in spiritual darkness and are cut off from God's life because their hearts are stubborn and hardened against Him. Because they have lost all sense of shame, they chase after every kind of moral impurity and always crave more.

The true way of Christ is completely opposite to that ungodly lifestyle. Those who have genuinely listened to Jesus and learned from Him know that He calls them away from sinful living. The real truth found in Jesus always leads to a transformed and pure character.

Believers are told to strip off their old sinful nature like dirty clothes, because its deceitful cravings lead only to ruin. At the same time, their inner thoughts and attitudes are being renewed by God's Spirit. Christians must put on their new self, which God created to reflect His own holy and righteous character.

Because believers are made new, they must stop lying and always speak truthfully to one another. Christians are all connected as fellow members of the same spiritual body. Deceiving another believer makes no more sense than one hand trying to trick the other.

If anger arises, believers must be careful not to let it lead them into sin. Anger should be dealt with quickly and not allowed to simmer overnight or turn into bitterness. Nursing grudges opens the door for the devil to gain a foothold and cause division in the church.

Anyone who used to steal must completely abandon theft and turn to honest, hard work. The purpose of working with our own hands is not just to provide for ourselves, but to have extra to share with those who cannot provide for themselves. Christian living replaces selfish taking with generous giving.

Foul or rotten language should never come out of a believer's mouth. Instead, words should be chosen carefully to encourage listeners and meet their specific spiritual needs at that moment. Gracious speech helps build others up rather than tearing them down.

Unholy words and sinful actions bring deep sorrow to the Holy Spirit, who lives within believers as a loving friend. God placed His Spirit inside His people as a permanent seal, guaranteeing their complete freedom on the day Christ returns. Out of love and respect for this divine seal, believers should avoid anything that grieves Him.

Christians must throw out all deep resentment, sudden outbursts of temper, and ongoing anger. Loud brawling, insulting words, and every wish to harm someone else have no place among God's people. Letting go of inward malice is the only way to stop these destructive habits from spilling into our relationships.

Believers are called to treat one another with warmth, deep sympathy, and tender hearts. They must forgive others freely whenever an offense occurs, holding no grudges. The greatest reason and pattern for our forgiveness is that God has already forgiven all our sins through Christ.
